memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In the first month the whole Israelite community arrived at the Desert of Zin, and they stayed at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried. — Num 20:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In a single, quiet sentence, Miriam's life comes to a close. She had been there from the very beginning — the sister who watched over the baby Moses in the reeds, who led the women in song after the Red Sea deliverance. Now, in the wilderness, she dies and is buried. The verse is brief, but the loss was surely deep.

There is something honest about how Scripture records grief without fanfare. Life's journey includes loss, and even the great figures of faith were not spared it. Miriam had walked with God's people through decades of wandering, and now her portion of the journey was complete. The community that had sung with her now buried her.

If you have lost someone dear, this verse quietly reminds you that grief is part of the road we all travel. God does not pretend otherwise. The wilderness of loss is real, and even faithful people pass through it. There is no shame in mourning; even Jesus wept at the grave of a friend.

Yet for those who belong to Christ, death does not have the final word. Miriam was buried in the wilderness, still short of the Promised Land — but the story of God's people did not end at her grave, and neither does ours. Jesus has conquered death, and for all who trust Him, the grave is not a full stop but a doorway. We grieve, but "not like the rest, who have no hope." One day every tear will be wiped away, and death itself will be no more. Carry your griefs to the God who understands them, and hold on to the hope that outlasts the grave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you experienced grief along your own journey?
2. How does it help to know Scripture treats loss and mourning honestly?
3. What hope does Christ's victory over death give you in the face of loss?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You understand grief and do not despise our tears. When loss comes, comfort me with Your presence and with the hope of resurrection in Christ. Thank You that the grave is not the end for those who trust You. Amen.
